- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too slowly — overshoots after sharp spikes in history.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the short term; prices often stay elevated longer than observed.
- When history shows a sharp drop (e.g., 45.93 → 34.33), model fails to adjust downward quickly — underestimates the drop’s magnitude.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to reflect volatility or sudden reversals in true outcomes.
- Model overreacts to recent high values — forecasts remain high even when true values are falling sharply.
- In cases of prolonged low prices, model fails to recognize the trend and continues to forecast upward.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market shocks — fails to adjust forecasts downward when true values dip unexpectedly.
- Forecasts often lag behind true values by 1–3 days, especially in the first 10 days of the 30d window.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to correct for recent downward trends unless they are very steep or sustained.
